ILLNESS AND MEDICATION  
   
20 Some illnesses that can affect driving  
20.3 Depression
Depression affects the capabilities of the driver:
Increasing distractions. The driver focuses all his attention on his thoughts and neglects the surroundings.
Making valuable information become lost or irrelevant. The driver fails to detect significant information needed for safety and requiring driver reaction, especially in more complex situations.
Increasing insecurity. Depression interferes in the decision-making process, so the driver can make mistakes or act unpredictably.
Increasing the propensity for sleepiness and fatigue. It is advisable not to drive at night or in environments where road monotony may occur or for long periods of time.
Increasing irritability and anxiety. A trivial event can provoke a disproportionate reaction by the driver.
In addition, there is usually the need for psychotropic drugs, which can directly affect the ability to drive.
(Página 48 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
Road traffic collisions  
   
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the enormous economic impact (either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs derived from road traffic accidents are classified as human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering. Material costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment. Healthcare costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations. Administrative costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.
(Página 248 del manual 'Learning to drive')

5 Overtaking  
5.8 Situations when you must not overtake
Nevertheless, in sections of roadway, where overtaking is prohibited, after verifying that the manoeuvre can be made without endangering any road user, it is possible to overtake:
pedestrians,
bicycles,
cycles,
mopeds,
animals and
vehicles pulled by animals
when, due to the speed they move at, they can be overtaken without risk to them or to general movement, even though to do so it is necessary to occupy the part of the road reserved for the opposite direction, after making sure that the manoeuvre can be carried out safely.
(Página 192 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS
 
15 The effects of alcohol in road traffic collisions
Alcohol is a psycho-depressive drug, that, even in small doses, negatively affects driving, disrupting the driver’s skills and abilities. It goes into the bloodstream and spreads throughout the body, affecting mainly the brain and the eyes.
(Página 40 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
3 Use of lanes  
 
3.3 Lanes located outside built-up-areas
On roads located outside built-upareas, where there are more than one lane for each direction of travel, driver of automobiles and special vehicles with a MAM in excess of 3,500 kg will normally drive in the lane located furthest to the right.
When traffic or road circumstances thus advise, you can use the rest of the lanes for your direction, provided that it does not obstruct another vehicle following you.
(Página 162 del manual 'Learning to drive')
